items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: I would consider it a privilege to appear before your organization with Nick LaRocca, comma, not only as his counsel, comma, and almost lifetime friend

ctx.x: Well, he wrote down to Mr. Howard Jacobs. He put a piece in the paper for asking for an old time jazz band to write him. That he was trying to clear up the great mystery that hangs over the jazz. That someone should get credit where it should be. Now many people ask, amongst this one was this Tom Brown and the record changer. Well, now these things I had never known before, the record changer, the claims that Brown made. These had just come to my mind. Now when you have a family to support you, just don't jump up…

It says, uh, CCE, DJ LaRocca, number 2218 Constant Street. October the 14th, 1957, I see. Heading of the letter, Mr. Harry V. Sushant, comma, President, New Orleans Jazz Club, comma, 2417 Octavia Street, New Orleans, Louisiana. Dear Harry, colon, for many months now, comma, I have delayed writing you concerning a matter, a matter, that I know means a great deal to you and the members of your organization, period. This matter means a great deal to me, comma, personally, comma, because one of the principal…
Now read Sushant. I'm reading it. I don't want to know them.

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-21
items.q: Sworn to and subscribed to before me this 12th day of June 1940, David L. Herman

ctx.x: came and appeared, Mrs. Alice, how do you pronounce her? Alice, Alice Kern. Alice Kern, K-I-E-R-N. A female person over the age of majority and full well known unto me notary public, who first being duly sworn, disposed and said as follows, that deponent was well acquainted with and has personally known for more than 25 years, one Dominic J. La Rocca, who resides in the city of New Orleans, state of Louisiana. A deponent is an organist by profession and during a period of time from 1914 to 1916, set down on paper…

Now, you wanted to ask me about the band that played in Bill Gallaty's band? This man could have been around my age, if he was living today, maybe a year too older than me. He may be the father of some of these Gallaty boys playing around today. That I don't know, because I have never met any of these boys. But they played in the downtown section. Bill Gallaty was the leader, or the manager of the band. And he played valve trombone. They had a boy by the name of Tots, I don't know his right name, played drums.…
